```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r preparing data}
# Install required packages if they are not already installed
packages <- c("ggplot2", "cluster", "dplyr", "knitr")

for (p in packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p)
  }
}

# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# Import the dataset
pharma <- read.csv("Pharmaceuticals.csv",
                   header = TRUE,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Examine the dataset
head(pharma)
str(pharma)
summary(pharma)

# Check dataset dimensions
dim(pharma)

# Save company identifiers
company_names <- pharma$Name
company_symbols <- pharma$Symbol

# Select the nine numerical variables
numeric_data <- pharma[, 3:11]

# Select the three categorical variables
categorical_data <- pharma[, 12:14]

# Check numerical variables
summary(numeric_data)

# Check for missing values
colSums(is.na(numeric_data))

# Check for variables with zero variance
sapply(numeric_data, sd)
```


```{r Standardize}
# Standardize numerical variables
scaled_data <- scale(numeric_data)

# Display standardized data
head(scaled_data)

# Check standardized means
round(colMeans(scaled_data), 3)

# Check standardized standard deviations
round(apply(scaled_data, 2, sd), 3)

# Verify there are no invalid values
anyNA(scaled_data)
any(is.infinite(scaled_data))
```



```{r Number of clusters}
# Calculate within-cluster sum of squares

wss <- numeric()

for (k in 1:8) {

  model <- kmeans(scaled_data,
                  centers = k,
                  nstart = 25)

  wss[k] <- model$tot.withinss

}

# Create elbow results
elbow_results <- data.frame(
  Clusters = 1:8,
  WSS = wss
)

# Display results
kable(elbow_results,
      digits = 3,
      caption = "Within-Cluster Sum of Squares")

# Plot elbow method
ggplot(elbow_results,
       aes(x = Clusters, y = WSS)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
  labs(title = "Elbow Method for Selecting Clusters",
       x = "Number of Clusters",
       y = "Within-Cluster Sum of Squares") +
  theme_minimal()


# Test cluster solutions from 2 through 6
silhouette_scores <- numeric()

for (k in 2:6) {



  model <- kmeans(scaled_data,
                  centers = k,
                  nstart = 25)

  sil <- silhouette(model$cluster,
                    dist(scaled_data))

  silhouette_scores[k - 1] <- mean(sil[, 3])

}

# Create silhouette results table
silhouette_results <- data.frame(
  Clusters = 2:6,
  Average_Silhouette = silhouette_scores
)

# Display results
kable(silhouette_results,
      digits = 3,
      caption = "Silhouette Analysis Results")

# Plot silhouette scores
ggplot(silhouette_results,
       aes(x = Clusters,
           y = Average_Silhouette)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:6) +
  labs(title = "Silhouette Analysis",
       x = "Number of Clusters",
       y = "Average Silhouette Width") +
  theme_minimal()

# Select the number of clusters with the highest silhouette score
best_k <- silhouette_results$Clusters[
  which.max(silhouette_results$Average_Silhouette)
]

# Display selected number of clusters
best_k
```

```{r Perform k-Means clustering}

# Perform k-Means clustering

final_model <- kmeans(
  scaled_data,
  centers = best_k,
  nstart = 25,
  iter.max = 100
)

# Display model results
final_model

# Add cluster assignments to the original dataset
pharma$Cluster <- as.factor(final_model$cluster)

# Create company assignment table
assignment_results <- data.frame(
  Symbol = company_symbols,
  Company = company_names,
  Cluster = pharma$Cluster
)

# Display company assignments
kable(assignment_results,
      caption = "Pharmaceutical Company Cluster Assignments")

# Display number of companies in each cluster
cluster_sizes <- as.data.frame(
  table(pharma$Cluster)
)

names(cluster_sizes) <- c(
  "Cluster",
  "Number_of_Companies"
)

kable(cluster_sizes,
      caption = "Companies in Each Cluster")

```

```{r Cluster averages}
kable(cluster_means,

names(cluster_sizes) <- c("Cluster", "Number_of_Companies")

kable(cluster_sizes,

```

```{r analysis}
# Combine original numerical variables with cluster assignments
profile_data <- numeric_data

profile_data$Cluster <- pharma$Cluster

# Calculate average financial characteristics by cluster
cluster_means <- profile_data %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(names(numeric_data)),
      ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Display cluster averages
kable(cluster_means,
      digits = 3,
      caption = "Average Financial Characteristics by Cluster")

# Calculate standardized cluster averages
scaled_profile <- as.data.frame(scaled_data)

scaled_profile$Cluster <- pharma$Cluster

standardized_means <- scaled_profile %>%
  group_by(Cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(names(numeric_data)),
      ~ mean(.x)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Display standardized cluster averages
kable(standardized_means,
      digits = 3,
      caption = "Standardized Financial Profiles by Cluster")

```

```{r visualize}
# Perform principal component analysis
pca_model <- prcomp(scaled_data,
                    center = FALSE,
                    scale. = FALSE)

# Create PCA visualization data
pca_data <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_model$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_model$x[, 2],
  Cluster = pharma$Cluster,
  Company = company_names
)

# Create PCA plot
ggplot(pca_data,
       aes(x = PC1,
           y = PC2,
           color = Cluster,
           label = Company)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.8,
            size = 2.5,
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Pharmaceutical Company Clusters",
       subtitle = "Principal Component Analysis",
       x = "Principal Component 1",
       y = "Principal Component 2",
       color = "Cluster") +
  theme_minimal()

# Display percentage of variance explained
summary(pca_model)

```

B

The results show that the three clusters have different financial characteristics. Cluster 1 has relatively low market capitalization, averaging 9.235, but has the highest revenue growth at 23.490%. It also has the highest leverage at 1.250. Overall, this cluster represents smaller companies that are growing quickly but rely more heavily on debt.

Cluster 2 contains the largest and most profitable companies. It has the highest market capitalization at 97.114, the highest return on equity at 35.7%, and the highest return on assets at 14.955%. It also has the highest net profit margin at 20.173% and the lowest beta at 0.434. This suggests that these companies are larger, more profitable, and have lower market risk.

Cluster 3 has the highest P/E ratio at 46.900, but the lowest revenue growth at 7.010%, return on equity at 11.3%, and net profit margin at 6.650%. This suggests that these companies have higher stock valuations but lower profitability and growth compared with the other clusters.

Overall, Cluster 1 represents smaller companies with strong growth and higher leverage. Cluster 2 represents larger, more profitable companies with lower risk. Cluster 3 represents companies with higher P/E ratios but weaker growth and profitability.


C
 
There are a few patterns in the clusters when looking at the remaining variables. Cluster 1 has the most Moderate Buy recommendations, while Cluster 2 has the most Hold recommendations. Cluster 3 is also mostly rated Hold.

For company location, Clusters 1 and 2 are mostly made up of US-based companies. Cluster 3 is more spread out, with companies from the US, Canada, Germany, and the UK.

For stock exchange, all companies in Clusters 2 and 3 are listed on the NYSE. Cluster 1 is also mostly NYSE-listed, with one AMEX company and one NASDAQ company.

Overall, there are some patterns in company location and stock exchange, but the recommendations are more mixed.


D

Cluster 1 – High-Growth, High-Leverage Companies - These companies have the strongest revenue growth but also rely more heavily on debt.

Cluster 2 – Large, Profitable Companies - These companies have the highest market capitalization and profitability, along with the lowest beta.

Cluster 3 – High-Valuation, Low-Growth Companies - These companies have the highest P/E ratios but lower revenue growth and profitability.
